newsitem.title: USA: Lehman profit margin widens in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Lehman profit margin widens in Q1.

text.p: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc said Monday its pre-tax profit margin widened to 23.7 percent in the fiscal first quarter ended in February, boosting net income to $144 million, or $1.16 per share.
The profit margin in the year-ago first quarter was 19.2 percent, and for all of 1996 it was 20.9 percent before a non-recurring charge in the fourth quarter.

Lehman said the first quarter was boosted by gains in strategically important high-margin businesses, including mergers and acquisitions, equity originations, derivatives, high-yield and emerging markets activities.
Net income in the first quarter was up 38 percent from a year earlier, and net income rose 47 percent.
"They beat everybody's estimate," said analyst Raphael Soifer of Brown Brothers Harriman. He was anticipating $0.95 per share, and Wall Street estimates ranged from $0.93 to $0.98.
Lehman reported a year-over-year 16 percent decline in principal transactions revenue, to $346 million.
Soifer said that when the $204 million in net interest income is added to the principal transactions revenue, it gives a clearer picture of trading.
